newsitem.title: USA: US needle distribution against AIDS rising.
newsitem.headline: US needle distribution against AIDS rising.

text.p: More than 14 million syringes were distributed last year through needle exchange programmes intended to prevent the spread of AIDS among intravenous drug users, federal health officials said Thursday.

The number of syringes exchanged in 1996 was a 75 percent increase from 1994, the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said. Almost half of the programmes were technically illegal but either operated underground or were tolerated by authorities.

About half of the 87 programmes surveyed in 28 states were in California, Washington, New York and Connecticut. The programmes exchanged about 14 million needles in 1996, compared with 11 million in 1995.

A 1994 study of New York City drug users concluded that regular participation in needle exchange programmes would cut in half the risk of infection with HIV, the virus that causes AIDS. About one-third of the nation's AIDS cases are related to the use of injecting drugs.

The Centre for AIDS Prevention Studies at the University of California San Franciso says needle exchange programmes cost about $9,400 per infection averted, well below the $119,000 lifetime cost of treating someone infected with HIV.
Supporters of needle exchange programmes say there is no evidence that they increase drug use.
